result.title: Answer or Defer? Testing VLMs' Stated Confidence on Brain MRI
result.comment: Accepted to the WACV 2027 FABRIC Workshop
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) could support medical-image interpretation, but their use requires deciding which interpretations to accept and which images to refer to a clinician. We test whether thresholding stated confidence can retain useful coverage while limiting errors among accepted answers, and how this depends on the population. Eight open-weight VLMs, including two reasoning models, assess 3,888 brain MRI slices from post-treatment glioma patients (BraTS 2024) and healthy volunteers (IXI) for tumor or gross abnormality. BraTS labels are mask-derived; IXI slices are treated as negatives. On BraTS, no threshold selects a nonempty set with at most 5% empirical error for any model, even when chosen retrospectively. This also holds for four models evaluated on a large-lesion, distant-negative subset. At a 10% error budget, Gemma-4-12B retains 24.4% of slices and every other model at most 2.5%. To investigate this limited selection ability, we separate confidence differences between predicted answers from differences within each answer. For four models with available outcome-level summaries, pooled mean confidence differs more between answers than between correct and incorrect responses within each answer. A covariance decomposition explains how this pattern can produce opposite confidence-correctness associations across populations. At a 20% error budget, accepting every "tumor" answer covers more slices than any confidence threshold for two models. These findings caution against using unvalidated stated confidence as a standalone deferral signal and support population-specific validation before deployment. Code is available at https://github.com/amir-sbg/VLM-Answer-or-Defer.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在脑 MRI 切片上评测八个开源 VLM，考察能否用陈述置信度阈值筛选可接受答案、将其余转交临床医生，并分析置信度与正确性的关联如何随人群变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及 VLM 的停止/转交决策与置信度校准；其阴性结果可供核查「依据置信度决定停止或继续推理」在分布变化下的可靠性，但未涉及 latent 状态或推理轨迹。
